question: Through which body does the Commission develop Union expertise and capabilities in artificial intelligence under the EU AI Act?
gold_answer: The Commission develops Union expertise and capabilities in the field of AI through the AI Office.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:64::1. The Commission shall develop Union expertise and capabilities in the field of AI through the AI Office.

question: Which European and national bodies may ask Union AI testing support structures for specialist guidance under the EU AI Act?
gold_answer: Union AI testing support structures must provide independent technical or scientific advice at the request of the Board, the Commission, or market surveillance authorities.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:84::2. Without prejudice to the tasks referred to in paragraph 1, Union AI testing support structures shall also provide independent technical or scientific advice at the request of the Board, the Commission, or of market surveillance authorities.

question: When an assessment organisation receives accreditation across several European laws, how many registration codes does the Commission issue under the EU AI Act?
gold_answer: The Commission assigns a single identification number to each notified body, even where that body is notified under more than one Union act.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:35::1. The Commission shall assign a single identification number to each notified body, even where a body is notified under more than one Union act.

question: Under the EU AI Act, what formal recording steps must be completed when participants agree to live trials outside regulatory sandboxes?
gold_answer: The informed consent must be dated and documented, and a copy must be provided to the subjects of testing or their legal representative.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:61::2. The informed consent shall be dated and documented and a copy shall be given to the subjects of testing or their legal representative.

question: Why does a standalone machine-learning model fall short of qualifying as a complete software application under the EU AI Act?
gold_answer: Although AI models are essential components of AI systems, they do not constitute AI systems on their own and require additional components, such as a user interface, to become AI systems.
gold_evidence: ai_act:rec:97::Although AI models are essential components of AI systems, they do not constitute AI systems on their own. AI models require the addition of further components, such as for example a user interface, to become AI systems.

question: What eligibility conditions must experts on the scientific panel meet under the EU AI Act, and when may that panel send a qualified alert to the AI Office?
gold_answer: Scientific panel experts must have particular AI scientific or technical expertise, be independent from AI system and general-purpose AI model providers, and be able to act diligently, accurately, and objectively. The panel may send a qualified alert to the AI Office when it suspects a general-purpose AI model poses concrete identifiable Union-level risk or meets systemic-risk classification conditions.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:68::(a) having particular expertise and competence and scientific or technical expertise in the field of AI; (b) independence from any provider of AI systems or general-purpose AI models; (c) an ability to carry out activities diligently, accurately and objectively. || ai_act:art:90::1. The scientific panel may provide a qualified alert to the AI Office where it has reason to suspect that: (a) a general-purpose AI model poses concrete identifiable risk at Union level; or (b) a general-purpose AI model meets the conditions referred to in Article 51.

question: At what stage must a developer compile technical documentation for a high-risk AI system under the EU AI Act, and how long must it retain those files for regulators?
gold_answer: The provider must draw up the technical documentation before the high-risk AI system is placed on the market or put into service and keep it up to date. The provider must keep it at the disposal of national competent authorities for 10 years after the system is placed on the market or put into service.

question: Who holds sole enforcement authority over foundation-model rules under the EU AI Act, and through what software channels can that enforcer inspect a model?
gold_answer: The Commission has exclusive powers to supervise and enforce general-purpose AI model obligations and entrusts implementation to the AI Office. When evaluating a model, the Commission may request access through APIs or other appropriate technical means and tools, including source code.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:88::1. The Commission shall have exclusive powers to supervise and enforce Chapter V, taking into account the procedural guarantees under Article 94. The Commission shall entrust the implementation of these tasks to the AI Office, without prejudice to the powers of organisation of the Commission and the division of competences between Member States and the Union based on the Treaties. || ai_act:art:92::3. For the purposes of paragraph 1, the Commission may request access to the general-purpose AI model concerned through APIs or further appropriate technical means and tools, including source code.

question: When do private-sector high-risk AI systems already launched before 2 August 2026 fall under the EU AI Act, and how is 'significant change' understood?
gold_answer: Non-public-authority high-risk AI systems (other than large-scale IT components) placed on the market before 2 August 2026 become subject to the EU AI Act only if they undergo significant changes in their designs from that date. The concept of significant change is understood as equivalent in substance to substantial modification.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:111::this Regulation shall apply to operators of high-risk AI systems, other than the systems referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article, that have been placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2026, only if, as from that date, those systems are subject to significant changes in their designs. || ai_act:rec:177::It is appropriate to clarify that, in this respect, the concept of significant change should be understood as equivalent in substance to the notion of substantial modification, which is used with regard only to high-risk AI systems pursuant to this Regulation.

question: When an overseas developer fine-tunes a foundation model for European release under the EU AI Act, what local representation step is needed, and how far do its provider duties extend?
gold_answer: Before placing the general-purpose AI model on the Union market, a third-country provider must appoint an authorised representative established in the Union by written mandate. Where a model is modified or fine-tuned, the provider's obligations are limited to that modification or fine-tuning, such as complementing existing technical documentation with modification details and new training data sources.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:54::1. question: Must every Member State build a brand-new national AI regulatory sandbox from scratch by 2 August 2026 under the EU AI Act?
gold_answer: Each Member State must ensure its competent authorities establish at least one national AI regulatory sandbox operational by 2 August 2026. However, that obligation may also be fulfilled by participating in an existing sandbox provided that participation gives an equivalent level of national coverage.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:57::1. Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities establish at least one AI regulatory sandbox at national level, which shall be operational by 2 August 2026. || ai_act:art:57::The obligation under the first subparagraph may also be fulfilled by participating in an existing sandbox in so far as that participation provides an equivalent level of national coverage for the participating Member States.

question: Must a provider's post-market monitoring system gather operational records from every user organisation deploying its high-risk AI product under the EU AI Act?
gold_answer: By default, the post-market monitoring system must actively and systematically collect, document, and analyse relevant performance data provided by deployers or other sources throughout the system's lifetime. However, this obligation does not cover sensitive operational data of deployers that are law-enforcement authorities.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:72::The post-market monitoring system shall actively and systematically collect, document and analyse relevant data which may be provided by deployers or which may be collected through other sources on the performance of high-risk AI systems throughout their lifetime || ai_act:art:72::This obligation shall not cover sensitive operational data of deployers which are law-enforcement authorities.

question: When a European regulator discovers missing conformity markings on a high-risk AI product under the EU AI Act, does it immediately ban the product from sale?
gold_answer: No; initially, the market surveillance authority must require the provider to end the formal non-compliance within a prescribed period. Only if the non-compliance persists must the authority restrict, prohibit, recall, or withdraw the high-risk AI system from the market.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:83::1. Where the market surveillance authority of a Member State makes one of the following findings, it shall require the relevant provider to put an end to the non-compliance concerned, within a period it may prescribe: (a) the CE marking has been affixed in violation of Article 48; (b) the CE marking has not been affixed; || ai_act:art:83::2. Where the non-compliance referred to in paragraph 1 persists, the market surveillance authority of the Member State concerned shall take appropriate and proportionate measures to restrict or prohibit the high-risk AI system being made available on the market or to ensure that it is recalled or withdrawn from the market without delay.

question: Under the EU AI Act, does relying on its compliance check for connected software override stricter safeguards for vital digital goods?
gold_answer: While the EU AI Act's conformity assessment procedure generally applies to essential cybersecurity requirements for covered products with digital elements classified as high-risk AI systems, that rule must not reduce the necessary level of assurance for critical products with digital elements.
gold_evidence: ai_act:rec:78::The conformity assessment procedure provided by this Regulation should apply in relation to the essential cybersecurity requirements of a product with digital elements covered by a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on horizontal cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements and classified as a high-risk AI system under this Regulation. || ai_act:rec:78::However, this rule should not result in reducing the necessary level of assurance for critical products with digital elements covered by a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on horizontal cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements.

question: What are the maximum validity periods for certificates of covered high-risk AI systems under the EU AI Act?
gold_answer: Conformity certificates may be valid for up to five years for AI systems covered by Annex I and up to four years for AI systems covered by Annex III.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:44::2. Certificates shall be valid for the period they indicate, which shall not exceed five years for AI systems covered by Annex I, and four years for AI systems covered by Annex III.

question: After an assessment body stops outsourcing work to an external contractor under the EU AI Act, how long must it retain the related qualification records?
gold_answer: The notified body must keep relevant documents on the subcontractor's or subsidiary's qualifications and work at the notifying authority's disposal for five years from the termination date of the subcontracting.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:33::4. The relevant documents concerning the assessment of the qualifications of the subcontractor or the subsidiary and the work carried out by them under this Regulation shall be kept at the disposal of the notifying authority for a period of five years from the termination date of the subcontracting.

question: When another country challenges a national enforcement step under the EU AI Act safeguard mechanism, what deadlines govern the Commission's final ruling?
gold_answer: The Commission must decide within six months of notification, or within 60 days in the case of non-compliance with prohibited AI practices.
gold_evidence: ai_act:art:81::On the basis of the results of that evaluation, the Commission shall, within six months, or within 60 days in the case of non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5, starting from the notification referred to in Article 79(5), decide whether the national measure is justified

gold_answer: The European Data Protection Supervisor and the European Data Protection Board delivered their joint opinion on 18 June 2021.

question: How does the EU AI Act structure the appeals procedure before the European AI Compensation Tribunal?
gold_answer: Not specified in the EU AI Act; the regulation does not establish a European AI Compensation Tribunal or any appeals procedure before such a body.
